statusText: Green - all 24 published hours fall inside the CME weekend halt, holding Tail at its structural floor
recommendation: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail remains far below the block threshold and no evidence-based danger window applies, because every published hour falls inside the CME weekend halt and no NQ price path can form. The 22:00Z Sunday futures reopen falls roughly nine hours beyond the final slot in this window. Existing-position management and emergency protection remain active as always.
headline: An unresolved Saudi pipeline repair timeline and cancelled October European cargoes wait out the weekend halt behind a 14.81 VIX and $100.30 crude, with Tail at its floor
body: Every hour published here falls inside the CME weekend halt. Cash equities closed at 20:00Z on Friday, the E-mini settled near 21:00Z, and equity futures do not reopen until 22:00Z on Sunday, roughly nine hours after the final slot in this window. Friday's marks were re-verified at primary sources for this assessment: the cash Nasdaq-100 settled at 29,644.17, up 197.17 points or 0.67% from a 29,447.00 previous close, finishing 3.6 points under the top of a 29,371.89-29,647.80 range and about 3.6% below its 30,762.20 fifty-two-week high; VIX fell 4.08% to 14.81 and settled at the low of a 14.80-15.63 range; WTI settled $100.30 (-1.58%) and Brent $103.87 (-0.91%), a third consecutive decline. Policy is the week's anchor and is already digested: the FOMC raised the target range 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on September 16 in a unanimous 12-0 vote, the first increase since July 2023, with sixteen of eighteen dot submissions showing at least one more. The H.15 observation for September 17 put the two-year at 4.67% and the ten-year at 4.94% against a 3.88% effective funds rate, so the curve prices policy well above the current setting. The open thread is Middle East supply. Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline, which normally moves 4-5 million barrels a day and exists to bypass the Strait of Hormuz, has been shut since September 11 after drone strikes from Iraq, and Hormuz itself has been constrained since the February 2026 escalation. Repair guidance remains genuinely unresolved between three-to-five weeks mostly out of service and an Aramco push to restore about half of capacity within days, and Aramco has told at least two European refiners they will receive no crude in October. Crude nonetheless fell on Friday, which is the informative reading: the market is discounting the outage commercially rather than chasing it. Friday was also quarterly quadruple witching alongside the Nasdaq-100 rebalance, so a close three points under the session high is better explained by expiry and reconstitution flow than by persistent momentum, and internal dispersion supports that - semiconductor equipment rose 4.85% and semis 1.87% while software fell about 1%, and megacaps split with AVGO up 2.97% against META down 2.43%. Because a halted contract cannot produce shallow pullbacks, failed retracements, repeated extension or session-extreme holding, Tail sits at its structural floor of 5 and lifts only to 6 from 07:00Z Sunday as untested headline exposure accumulates toward a reopen that still falls outside this window. Stress drifts from 22 to 25 and Confidence steps from 75 to 62 on evidence ageing rather than observed difficulty. Mapped policy state: EA_ON, with no evidence-based danger window applicable. Existing-position management and emergency protection remain active as always.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly assessments were published and every one mapped to green. Tail ran 16-18 through Friday's dispersed U.S. cash session, then fell through 16, 11, 7 and 6 as trading ended and the contract settled, holding 5 across the final fourteen hours. Stress peaked at 51 in the U.S. afternoon and decayed through 44, 33, 28 and 26 into the halt, bottoming at 21 for five consecutive slots before settling at 22. Confidence held between 75 and 88, easing only once the halt removed any refreshing observation. Dominant mode was mixed across the cash session, turned trend-up into the close, then normal for the whole post-settlement stretch.
outlookSummary: All 24 published slots fall inside the weekend halt: cash closed at 20:00Z Friday, the E-mini printed last near 21:00Z, and CME equity futures do not reopen until 22:00Z Sunday, roughly nine hours after the final slot here. Tail holds 5 through Saturday and the Sunday small hours and lifts to 6 from 07:00Z as untested weekend headline exposure accumulates ahead of the reopen; that single point reflects proximity and accumulated unpriced time, never observed structure. Stress drifts from 22 to 25, crossing into the moderate band late on staleness alone, and Confidence steps from 75 to 62 for the same reason. Dominant mode is normal throughout, because a closed market cannot express a trend. The conditional routes to a reopen gap are the unresolved Saudi East-West repair timeline, the cancelled October European allocations, the rates path after a hike that left the ten-year near 4.94%, and any weekend policy commentary. The Saudi Exchange Sunday session, roughly 07:00-12:00Z, is the only venue able to price the pipeline file before this window closes. No CPI, NFP, PCE or FOMC falls inside the next seven days; the first hard checkpoint is Wednesday's S&P Global flash PMIs at 13:45Z.
